title: The Present Indicative Active — Fourth and Mixed
subtitle: audiō, capiō. The -iō verbs and the i-stem class.
objectives: Distinguish fourth from third i-stem by infinitive.
Translate sentences with all four conjugations.

sections.heading: Fourth conjugation and third i-stem
sections.body:
The fourth conjugation has infinitives in -īre: audīre (to hear). Theme vowel: -ī- (long i).

Fourth conjugation:
  audiō, audīs, audit, audīmus, audītis, audiunt

The third conjugation i-stem verbs (also called 'mixed' conjugation) look like fourth but have infinitives in -ĕre: capere (to take, to seize).

Third i-stem:
  capiō, capis, capit, capimus, capitis, capiunt

Caesar writes: oppidum capiunt. — They seize the town.
Cicero writes: verba audīmus. — We hear the words.

items.prompt: Conjugate sentiō (to feel, 4th) in all persons.
items.answer: sentiō, sentīs, sentit, sentīmus, sentītis, sentiunt

items.prompt: Conjugate faciō (to do/make, 3rd i-stem) in all persons.
items.answer: faciō, facis, facit, facimus, facitis, faciunt
Infinitive: 4th ends in -īre (long i), 3rd i-stem ends in -ĕre (short e).

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark complete when you can conjugate audiō and capiō and distinguish them by infinitive.
